key_insight: The paper studies the limits of building a multiclass classifier by combining only O(log K) simple binary decisions. In particular, it shows how far a distributed classifier based on hyperplane-based binary classifiers can go in a stylized Gaussian setting.
problem_solved: How can we reliably construct a K-class classifier from a small number of simple binary classifiers in a distributed setting, and what are the fundamental accuracy limits of this approach?
method: Model each binary decision as a hyperplane classifier.
Analyze a hierarchical/combined decision scheme that uses only O(log K) binary classifiers to distinguish K classes.
Study performance limits in a stylized Gaussian class-center model to characterize when the approach succeeds or fails.
impact: This work gives practitioners a principled understanding of the tradeoff between classifier simplicity, scalability, and accuracy in distributed AI systems. It can guide the design of lightweight multi-agent or edge-based classification pipelines where each component must make only a simple binary decision.
visual_elements: Tree diagram showing K classes reduced to a sequence of binary splits
Illustration of distributed agents each making a hyperplane-based yes/no decision
Gaussian scatter plot of class centers with separating hyperplanes
Tradeoff chart showing number of binary decisions versus classification accuracy
paper_title: Fundamental limits of distributed multiclass classification from simple binary decisions
paper_authors: Ioannis Papageorgiou, Srinivas Nomula, Ayalvadi Ganesh, Sidharth Jaggi, Parimal Parag
